[LSTO.4.7.5] **The cache may be bounded.** An integration may bound the
cache by the number of its live keys and by the total bytes of its values.
Neither bound is set by default, and an unbounded cache refuses no write. A
bound binds the writes and seeds that follow its setting and evicts nothing; it
never changes during a pump.

A `cache` write of a key the cache does not hold, when it already holds as many
live keys as the key bound allows, or a write that would leave more value bytes
than the byte bound allows, is a bounds refusal ([LERR.1.5]).
The engine must not perform the write. It records a `BoundsError` naming the
bound and stops the firing at the write, by the prefix rule of [LNUL.11.1]: the
actions before it stand, and the actions after it do not run. The pump goes on
and returns `DS_ERR_CONTRACT_BREACH`, and a later `cached()` reads the cache as
it was before the refused write.

A cache seed ([LSTO.4.7.4]) is charged against the same bounds. A seed past
either bound is refused with `DS_ERR_CONTRACT_BREACH` and leaves the cache
unchanged.

A bound changes what `cached()` reads, so it is engine configuration that a
replay must reproduce ([LDET.2.7]).
